newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - RPIX to drop below 2.5 pct this year.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - RPIX to drop below 2.5 pct this year.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Sunday that underlying inflation will drop below his government's target of 2.5 percent this year.
There was little difference between him and the Bank of England over interest rates, he added.

"Inflation now is coming down towards 2.5 percent, it's going to go through that in the course of this year," he said in a three-way BBC television debate with his Labour counterpart Gordon Brown and Liberal Democrat finance spokesman Malcolm Bruce.

Clarke, who meets with Bank of England Governor Eddie George this week for their monthly discussion of monetary policy, said the gap between him and George amounted to just one quarter of a percentage point. George has pressed for base rates to be raised to 6.25 percent throughout this year.
"When we had Labour chancellors in the past they would have given their eye teeth to talk about figures of inflation and interest rates that we now have," Clarke said.
Retail price inflation figures will be released a week on Thursday. In February, it stood at 2.9 percent year-on-year.
